title: Peter's bold promise and the Spirit not yet given
english: If Peter had asked him, perhaps he would not have denied him once the servant-girls were removed. For it could not have happened that, when the question was put to him, he would confess the Lord in the Holy Spirit, since the Holy Spirit had not yet been given. His bold promise became the reason he not only stumbled but denied him three times.
translator_notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is reflecting on Peter's predicted denial, explaining why Peter could not have confessed Christ in the Holy Spirit at that moment.

title: Could Peter's denial have been averted by prayer?
english: "Truly I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times" (Matthew 26:34). The question is raised whether, if Peter had prayed that the foreknown denial be driven away, he might not have denied him after all—just as God, having been entreated by the Ninevites, did not do what he had foretold through Jonah (Jonah 3:10). Glory to Christ. Amen.
translator_notes: Series rem denial from PG 13 Latin.
orientation: Origen is still discussing Peter's predicted denial, now asking whether Peter could have prayed to have the foreknown denial turned away, as Nineveh's repentance turned away Jonah's announced destruction.
